title: Zelenskyy Slams Trump’s Russian Diesel Deal as Deadly Bombings Kill 15 in Ukraine
snippet: Russian aerial strikes devastated Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region on Saturday, leaving at least 15 dead just one day after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a controversial energy deal with Moscow.
content:
KYIV, Ukraine — Russian forces launched a series of brutal aerial bombardments across Ukraine on Saturday, killing at least 15 people in the Zaporizhzhia region—including three children—just hours after U.S. President Donald Trump announced a landmark agreement to import Russian diesel fuel.

The barrage hit residential communities with heavy glide bombs, injuring at least 16 others in Zaporizhzhia while a daylight missile attack in Kyiv left four wounded. The attacks mark a sharp escalation in a conflict that has claimed more than 60 Ukrainian lives over the past four days alone.

Zelenskyy Condemns Energy Pact as 'Weak Decision'

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reacted with fierce criticism to both the strikes and the surprise trade deal between Washington and Moscow, arguing that easing economic sanctions directly funds Russia's war machine.

“Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media, warning that relaxing diplomatic and economic pressure signals to Moscow that it can continue attacking cities without consequence.

Zelenskyy also voiced frustration over concurrent peace discussions in Miami involving Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, suggesting the diplomatic outreach was being used as a "smoke screen" while Moscow gains vital financial lifelines.

Trump Eyes Lower Gas Prices Ahead of Midterms

The announcement from Washington represents a significant pivot in U.S. foreign policy. Aiming to reduce domestic fuel prices ahead of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections, President Trump revealed that Russia will immediately supply 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by millions of additional tons in the near future.

The move stands in stark contrast to previous sanctions aimed at choking off Kremlin energy revenues. On the streets of Kyiv, citizens expressed anger and fatigue over the announcement, viewing the deal as a transactional strategy that puts American political gains ahead of Ukrainian survival.
